boundaries: unordered or swapped bounds are not clamp-equivalent
float or NaN-sensitive domains stay outside this integer clamp pattern
method names alone do not prove library clamp semantics
custom clamp-shaped APIs need receiver, domain, and bound-order evidence

language_surfaces.surface: min(max(x, lo), hi), max(min(x, hi), lo), and guarded ternary clamp
integer .clamp(lo, hi) when literal or guard evidence proves lo <= hi
generic min/max Constrain-style helpers after integer-domain and bound-order proof
number-domain min/max clamp forms until float/NaN boundaries are excluded

patterns.law: Integer clamp surfaces are equivalent only when they compute the same bounded value and source evidence proves both integer-domain operands and lo <= hi bound order.
patterns.rationale: The numeric-clamp packet already has a proof-carrying perimeter, modeled facts, focused positives, and hard negatives; recording it as a semantic pattern makes future language surfaces attach to the same invariant instead of to min/max or method-name spelling.
patterns.title: Proof-backed integer clamp

boundaries: absent-key fallback is distinct from nullish, truthy, or falsey value replacement
the map receiver must be the same proven source, including imported immutable literal sources
the lookup key and fallback/default coordinates must match independently
receiver mutation between construction/import, guard, and lookup is behavior-defining

language_surfaces.surface: dict.get and membership-guarded literal/imported map lookup
named imports from unmutated sibling map/object exports
static Map.of field imports with getOrDefault-style absence fallback
use-imported const entry arrays consumed by HashMap::from
Dictionary default subscript after receiver-coordinate proof

patterns.law: Map-default lookup surfaces are equivalent only when they read the same stable map source with the same key and fallback, and the fallback is proven to mean absent-key behavior.
patterns.rationale: The frontier platform records map_default_lookup as a high-breadth multi-language candidate with focused cross-file evidence and adjacent mutation/wrong-map negatives; carding it keeps future work on map semantics instead of API spelling.
patterns.title: Absence-preserving map default lookup

boundaries: the drop condition is independent from the emitted value expression
None/Null/Nil absence drops an element, but falsey present payloads are still emitted
wrapped absence payloads such as Some(None) remain present payloads in nested option domains
observed callback effects and evaluation timing are behavior-defining

language_surfaces.surface: filtered comprehensions as explicit drop-condition plus emitted-value surfaces
filter().map() chains with the same predicate and mapped value coordinates
Iterator::filter_map with Some/None, match guards, and pure Option::and_then callbacks
Sequence.compactMap after optional-result channel and callback-effect proof

patterns.law: Filter-map style surfaces are equivalent to explicit filter+map or guarded builders only when they traverse the same source, drop the same elements through a proven absence channel, emit the same present value, and callback effects are closed.
patterns.rationale: The hof_filter_map corpus already contains cross-language positives plus hard negatives for None-as-value, changed payloads, falsey payloads, wrapped None payloads, and effectful callbacks; carding the pattern makes future compactMap/filter_map work attach to optional-emission facts instead of per-language API names.
patterns.title: Optional-emission filter-map
